The event was the eighth annual Turkey Ride, organised through a partnership between Maine Sport Rockport and the Camden Area Christian Food Pantry. According to WABI, 58 families received a turkey free of charge for their Thanksgiving dinner.

Article Title: An Illinois World War II veteran who fought in Europe at 18 and helped liberate Dachau has received France’s Legion of Honor at 102; he still lives independently and drives, more than eight decades af
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A 102-year-old World War II veteran from Illinois, who fought in Europe at the age of 18 and helped liberate the Dachau concentration camp in Germany, has received France’s prestigious Legion of Honor. William Lyford, a resident of Woodstock, was presented with the distinction on November 13 in recognition of his service during the war. According to ABC7 Chicago, which reported the ceremony, Lyford continues to live independently in his home and still drives, more than eight decades after returning from the battlefield.The ceremony brought together Lyford's family, friends and fellow veterans to recognise his contribution to the Allied efforts during World War II. The French government awarded him the Legion of Honor, France's highest national distinction, in recognition of his role in helping liberate the country from Nazi occupation. The honour also acknowledges the sacrifices made by American servicemen who fought alongside French forces and their allies during the conflict.Lyford was just 18 when he served in Europe in 1945. His wartime service included time in France towards the end of the conflict, as well as participation in the liberation of Dachau, one of Nazi Germany's most notorious concentration camps, located near Munich.His military record already includes several American decorations, including the Bronze Star and the Combat Infantry Badge.The liberation of Dachau remains one of the defining moments of the final months of World War II. Established by the Nazi regime in March 1933, Dachau was the first regular concentration camp and became a model for the wider network of camps that followed. It held political prisoners, Jewish people and others persecuted by the Nazis, with inmates subjected to forced labour, starvation, disease and systematic brutality.According to the United States Holocaust Memorial Museum, American forces liberated Dachau on April 29, 1945. Soldiers from the 42nd and 45th Infantry Divisions and the 20th Armored Division took part in the operation, freeing approximately 32,000 prisoners. As they approached the camp, American troops encountered overwhelming evidence of Nazi atrocities, including railway cars filled with the bodies of prisoners who had died during transportation.The liberation came as Allied forces advanced deeper into Germany and the Nazi regime approached defeat. For survivors who had endured years of imprisonment, the arrival of American soldiers marked the end of captivity, although many were left severely weakened by hunger, disease and abuse.For Lyford, the experience was part of his service as an infantryman during the final phase of the war in Europe. He left the military in 1945 and returned to civilian life in the United States. He subsequently built a career in construction contracting, moving away from the battlefields and towards a profession that would occupy much of his post-war life.More than 80 years later, his daughter April Kopplin travelled from Colorado to attend the ceremony in Woodstock. She recalled that her father rarely spoke about his wartime experiences while she was growing up. His military past was not something the family regularly discussed, and she occasionally came across photographs from that period instead."Once in a while. I'd see a picture in a box in the house somewhere. That was it. They just didn't make a big deal out of it. They came home and made a life for themselves," Kopplin told ABC7 Chicago.Despite his age, Lyford continues to maintain an independent lifestyle. He remains in his Woodstock home and still drives, a detail that has drawn attention alongside the recognition of his wartime service. His longevity also made the occasion particularly significant for the local veterans' community.John Widmayer, a Vietnam veteran, expressed pride in Lyford's achievement and his continued presence among the community's surviving veterans. "Our VFW is very proud of him. There aren't many post that can say they have a 102 year old veteran infantryman still alive," Widmayer said.French Consul General Charlotte Mantel also attended the event and spoke about the significance of recognising veterans who helped secure France's freedom during the war. She said Lyford's contribution reflected the enduring alliance between the two countries. "What Mr Lyford did during the second world war was showcasing what this alliance means. We are so grateful for what he did," Mantel said.The Legion of Honor was established on May 19, 1802, by Napoleon Bonaparte and remains France's highest national decoration. According to the French institution responsible for administering the order, it recognises individuals for outstanding merit and contributions to the public good.While it is awarded to both military personnel and civilians, it has also been used to recognise foreign veterans who played a role in France's liberation during World War II.For Lyford, the recognition was something he had never expected to receive. Reflecting on the honour, he told ABC7 Chicago: "This is truly an honor that I never dreamt of." He also revealed that he planned to place the medal on his pillow when he went to sleep that night, marking a personal moment after a lifetime that had taken him from the battlefields of Europe to a quiet home in Illinois.
Article Summary: William Lyford was just 18 when he served in Europe in 1945. He helped liberate Dachau, one of Nazi Germany's most notorious concentration camps. The French government awarded him the Legion of Honor, France's highest national distinction. Lyford continues to live independently in his home and still drives.

With approximately an hour remaining before the scheduled arrival in Tampa, the pilot consulted her about diverting. She recommended Charlotte because the passenger needed medical assessment and treatment that could not be provided adequately during the flight.The aircraft landed there, and emergency medical personnel took over the passenger's care.American Airlines later recognised the nurse practitioner's efforts by awarding her 25,000 AAdvantage miles. Article Title: Redrawing Pakistan: Ministers back 12-province plan but political, constitutional hurdles remain
Article Text:
Pakistan's 12-province proposal gains momentum as senior ministers back restructuring (Representative Image)

What the proposed 12-province map could look like

Political consensus remains the biggest hurdle

What the Constitution requires

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Pakistan's proposal to expand its four-province structure to as many as 12 has gathered momentum, with senior ministers backing it in the name of better governance. But the idea faces a major political hurdle: there is no consensus among the country's leading parties, particularly over the possible division of Sindh.Pakistan’s defence minister Khawaja Asif has argued that Pakistan's growing population requires smaller provinces that can deliver public services more efficiently. Speaking to Geo News, he said the country could consider creating 12 provinces, provided the boundaries were drawn on administrative rather than linguistic, ethnic or political grounds.“If there is a proposal for 12 provinces, then make it 12,” Asif said, adding that new units should not be created to serve “language, ethnicity or political interests”.Pakistan’s interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi has also revived the debate, suggesting a referendum to gauge public opinion on the contentious issue. His remarks have fuelled speculation that powerful quarters favour a broader restructuring of Pakistan's administrative map, with reports pointing to a possible constitutional exercise in 2027.No formal roadmap, however, has been announced. The proposed number of provinces, their boundaries and the process for creating them remain undecided.One proposal reported in Pakistani media envisages dividing Punjab into four provinces, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan into three each, and Sindh into two. The plan could involve a nationwide referendum and a possible 28th Constitutional Amendment, although neither has been confirmed as an approved government initiative.Supporters argue that the existing arrangement concentrates too much administrative and financial authority in provincial capitals leaving smaller cities and districts dependent on decisions taken far away.Asif has questioned whether federal funds transferred to provincial governments are reaching local institutions, arguing that decentralisation could bring decision-making and resources closer to communities. Advocates of the proposal say smaller provinces would make public services more accessible and help address uneven development.But the debate is not only about the size of administrative units. It also raises questions about whether creating more provinces would improve governance without stronger local governments and greater financial autonomy for districts.The proposal has exposed differences within the ruling coalition itself. The Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP), led by Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari, has firmly opposed any division of Sindh, while the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) has yet to settle on a formal position.The two parties are coalition partners in the federal government. The PML-N has said it will announce its position if the matter comes before Parliament, despite some of its leaders backing the creation of smaller provinces.A cabinet member in the Shehbaz Sharif government said reaching agreement would be difficult without the support of the major political parties.The issue has also prompted speculation about a possible understanding between the government and the main opposition, Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI). PML-N leader and former federal minister Khawaja Saad Rafique has suggested that the establishment could offer relief to jailed former prime minister Imran Khan in return for PTI's support for the proposed constitutional changes. There has been no confirmation of such a deal.Smaller parties have also entered the debate. The Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) has renewed its demand for new administrative units in Sindh, while Pakistan Muslim League-Quaid chief Chaudhry Shujaat Hussain has called for new provinces to be considered through consultation and in the national interest.The Istehkam-e-Pakistan Party has backed the proposal on administrative grounds, while Jamaat-i-Islami has argued that the creation of new provinces should go hand in hand with strengthening local governments.Even if political parties agree on the broad idea, redrawing provincial boundaries would require a demanding constitutional process.Under Article 239 of Pakistan's Constitution, an amendment requires the support of at least two-thirds of the total membership of both houses of Parliament. If it changes the limits of an existing province, it must also secure the backing of at least two-thirds of the total membership of that province's assembly.That gives provincial parties considerable leverage over any proposed division.A nationwide referendum is not an automatic constitutional requirement for creating provinces. Any such exercise would need its own legal and constitutional basis, and Parliament could not simply be bypassed in deciding the process or framing the questions put to voters.Following a meeting between Pakistan’s president Asif Ali Zardari and prime minister Shehbaz Sharif on Saturday, a senior government official told news agency PTI that the two leaders had agreed to adhere strictly to the constitutional provisions governing the creation of new provinces. They also agreed that any proposed referendum would require parliamentary approval.Former federal information minister Muhammad Ali Durrani has meanwhile launched a campaign for the restoration of Bahawalpur province and the creation of 11 other smaller administrative units.For now, the proposal remains a subject of political debate rather than an agreed government plan. Any move to redraw the map would require agreement on boundaries, resources, parliamentary representation and the future of provincial institutions — as well as the constitutional numbers to make it happen.
Article Summary: Pakistan’s defence minister Khawaja Asif has argued that Pakistan's growing population requires smaller provinces that can deliver public services more efficiently. But the idea faces a major political hurdle: there is no consensus among the country's leading parties, particularly over the possible division of Sindh.

Article Title: 24 militants, four soldiers killed in separate clashes in Pakistan's Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
Article Text:
(Photo credit: IANS)

At least 24 militants and four Pakistani soldiers, including an army officer, were killed in separate encounters between security forces and militants in Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa provinces, the Pakistan Army said on Saturday, PTI reported.The army said security forces had carried out multiple intelligence-based operations (IBOs) in Balochistan since Friday, targeting militant hideouts in the areas of Kolpur, Kardagap and Nushki.During an operation in Kolpur on the intervening night of Friday and Saturday, troops killed eight militants, including a suicide bomber, and recovered a large cache of weapons and ammunition, the military said.The army said the militants used armed quadcopters to target military vehicles on patrol. The attack killed Major Omer Minhas Nasir and Havildar Muhammad Adnan Khan.The Pakistani government last year designated terrorist groups operating in Balochistan as 'Fitna al Hindustan'. Islamabad has alleged that these outfits carry out terrorist activities at India's behest, but has not provided evidence to support the claim.In June, India criticised Pakistan at the United Nations over the use of the term, calling it "officially sponsored misinformation and disinformation dressed in religious terminology."Separately, security forces conducted operations against militant hideouts in Mir Ali, Datta Khel and surrounding areas of North Waziristan district in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.According to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), the military's media wing, 16 militants were killed in the engagements. Twelve were killed in an operation in Ali Khel, while two each were killed in Mir Ali and Datta Khel.Two soldiers, Havildar Asmat Ali and Naik Aftab Ali, were killed during the operations. The ISPR said both soldiers fought bravely and laid down their lives in the line of duty. It added that the operations had dealt a major blow to the militant network.Weapons and ammunition were recovered from the slain militants, who, according to the military, were involved in several terrorist activities, including the killing of civilians.Pakistan's federal government uses the term 'Fitna al-Khawarij' for militants belonging to the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP).
Article Summary: At least 24 militants and four Pakistani soldiers killed in Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa provinces. Security forces carried out multiple intelligence- based operations (IBOs) since Friday, targeting militant hideouts in the areas of Kolpur, Kardagap and Nushki. During an operation in Kolpur on the intervening night of Friday and Saturday, troops killed eight militants.

A 19-year-old Pakistani teenager was mauled to death by a tigress after it was let out of its cage for a TikTok video shoot.The victim, identified as Talha, was working at a private breeding facility in Kahna, Lahore district, when the animal attacked him. He was rushed to a private hospital but died while undergoing treatment on Wednesday, according to local reports.Police identified the arrested farm owner as Fayyaz and the TikToker as Noman. It said all aspects of the alleged negligence and the attempt to conceal the attack would be investigated.There has been some confusion in initial media reports over whether the animal was a tiger or a lion. Article Title: Imran Khan-Asim Munir deal? Sisters' release from jail, hospital visit spark buzz in Pakistan
Article Text:
Release of Imran Khan's two sisters and his hospital visit fuel speculation of a possible political understanding with Pakistan's military establishment

PTI ready to make peace?

Nawaz Sharif , Benazir Bhutto precedent

Why a deal may not be straightforward

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Is Pakistan witnessing the first signs of a possible thaw between jailed former prime minister Imran Khan and the country's powerful military establishment? The release of two of his sisters and his recent hospital visit for eye treatment have come amid speculation that a political settlement involving Army Chief Field Marshal Asim Munir has taken place.His sisters, Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi were released on Thursday from Lahore's Kot Lakhpat Jail after the Punjab government withdrew their extended detention orders. The two had spent 53 days in custody after being detained ahead of a Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) protest march. Their sister Aleema Khan remains behind bars.The release came a day after Imran Khan was taken from Adiala Jail to Islamabad's Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences for an eye examination and treatment. Doctors administered an injection for an issue affecting his right eye, besides treating his blood pressure. He was discharged in the early hours of Thursday and returned to prison.The developments have coincided with renewed speculation about a possible deal involving Khan and the military establishment. Pakistan interior minister Mohsin Naqvi, however, dismissed reports of any behind-the-scenes arrangement on Thursday, saying Khan and his family would receive whatever relief the courts granted them.The possibility of a rapprochement is not entirely new. In August, one of Imran Khan's closest aides, PTI spokesperson Zulfikar Bukhari, had told Reuters that the former prime minister would not confront the military if released."If Imran Khan was released tomorrow, hypothetically, he wouldn't do anything that would effectively damage the country," Bukhari had said, describing him as "magnanimous".He had also suggested that Munir could take the initiative to ease tensions, saying the army chief could extend a "healing hand" to the country."That doesn't mean you go loggerheads with the establishment, with the military leader," Bukhari said, adding that personal grievances could be set aside in the national interest.The remarks marked a notable shift in the PTI's public rhetoric after years of confrontation with the military establishment following Khan's ouster in a no-confidence vote in 2022.Bukhari, however, had mentioned that there were no talks between the PTI and the military. He also acknowledged that it was unclear whether Khan himself shared the willingness to reconcile being expressed by party leaders outside prison.The latest speculation has also been fuelled by opposition leader Mahmood Khan Achakzai's claim in October that Khan could be facing pressure to accept an arrangement similar to those involving former prime ministers Nawaz Sharif and Benazir Bhutto.Sharif left Pakistan in 2000 after being ousted and imprisoned following the military coup led by General Pervez Musharraf. Bhutto spent years abroad in self-imposed exile after her government was dismissed in 1996.Achakzai alleged that the ruling Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz and Pakistan Peoples Party were part of a political arrangement that could pave the way for a similar outcome in Khan's case. However, he did not establish that any such agreement had been reached.An exile arrangement could potentially offer a way out of the prolonged confrontation, but there is no confirmation that Khan has agreed to leave Pakistan or that negotiations with Munir are under way.Imran Khan's relationship with the military establishment deteriorated after disagreements over key appointments and foreign policy. He has accused the military leadership, including Munir, of orchestrating his removal. The military denies interfering in politics.Despite being in prison since August 2023, Khan remains the central figure in Pakistan's political confrontation. His party continues to demand his release, access to family members and lawyers, and relief in the cases against him.The PTI's position also raises a crucial question: can its leadership outside prison negotiate or signal a compromise without Khan's explicit approval? Bukhari's August remarks came with the caveat that the former prime minister's own thinking might be different.For now, the signals remain contradictory. Two members of Khan's family have been released, he has received medical treatment, and a senior PTI aide has previously spoken of reconciliation. But the government has denied any political bargain, and there is no evidence of direct negotiations with Munir.Whether the latest developments represent isolated legal and medical decisions or the beginning of a fresh political opening remains the question.
Article Summary: Imran Khan's two sisters were released from jail on Thursday after 53 days in custody. He was also taken to a hospital for an eye examination and treatment. The developments have fuelled speculation about a possible deal involving Khan and the military establishment. Pakistan interior minister dismissed reports of any behind-the-scenes arrangement on Thursday.

Article Title: BLA claims 18 killed in suicide vehicle attack on Pakistan Army camp in Balochistan
Article Text:
Baloch Liberation Army claims responsibility for a suicide vehicle attack on a Pakistani Army camp in Balochistan, claiming 18 personnel were killed

NEW DELHI: Multiple casualties were reported in a VBIED attack at Pak army’s main camp in Mastung, Balochistan Thursday. The Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) took responsibility for the attack, claiming to have eliminated 18 personnel.According to BLA, its Fidayeen attack, the Majeed Brigade, carried out an operation in the Kanak area of Mastung, targeting a Pakistani military camp with a suicide vehicle-borne improvised explosive device followed by an assault by its armed fighters who entered the premises and targeted military personnel.The attack unfolded while a meeting of senior Pak Army personnel including colonel rank officials was underway when the mini-truck laden with explosives rammed into the main gate of the camp.The area has been on the boil since Wednesday. According to pro-BLA accounts on Telegram, Pak security forces were carrying out “operation Radd-ul-Fitna”, aimed at destroying tunnels allegedly made by Baloch rebels, on Wednesday and Thursday in the area.They claimed to have destroyed seven tunnels and seized arms, ammunition and explosives. In Musakhel, unidentified set ablaze construction machinery and a separate explosion destroyed a bridge in Mastung.On Wednesday, 13 Pakistani police personnel including a Deputy Superintendent of Police were killed after fighters from the rebel group Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) launched a major attack targeting mobile police units in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
Article Summary: The Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) took responsibility for the attack, claiming to have eliminated 18 personnel. The attack unfolded while a meeting of senior Pak Army personnel including colonel rank officials was underway when the mini-truck laden with explosives rammed into the main gate of the camp.

Article Title: 'Some good news': Two sisters of ex-Pak PM Imran Khan released from jail; elder sister, wife remain behind bars
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Two sisters of Pakistan's incarcerated former Prime Minister Imran Khan were released from a Lahore jail on Thursday after the Punjab government revoked their detention orders, leaders of his Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI) party said.However, his elder sister and wife remain behind bars."Finally, some good news. Two of former PM Imran Khan's sisters, Dr Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi, have been released from Kot Lakhpat Jail following the withdrawal of their detention orders," PTI senior leader and former federal minister Moonis Elahi said in a statement."Hopefully, Aleema sahiba and Bushra Bibi, will also be released soon," he added, referring to the cricketer-turned-politician's elder sister and wife, respectively.Meanwhile, another senior PTI leader, Zulfi Bokhari, asserted that the release of Imran Khan's two sisters would not "erase the suffering" endured by his family."The release of two sisters does not end the injustice or erase the suffering inflicted on Imran Khan’s family. The demand is clear -- no selective relief, no intimidation, and no further persecution," Bokhari told party supporters.Imran Khan's sisters were detained in September under a public safety law to prevent them from mobilising support for a nationwide protest demanding his release.Bushra Bibi was arrested in January 2025 in a separate case in which the couple were sentenced.The 74-year-old PTI founder has been in prison since 2023 and faces more than 100 cases, including corruption charges and allegations of inciting violence.On Wednesday, PTI lawyers met Imran Khan at Rawalpindi's Adiala Jail to discuss his ongoing court cases, a day after the Islamabad high court directed authorities to facilitate the meeting.The lawyers spent four hours at the prison before leaving without speaking to the media.According to PTI lawyer Latif Khosa, who was part of the delegation, Imran Khan was experiencing problems with his blood pressure and eyesight.
Article Summary: Two sisters of Pakistan's incarcerated former PM Imran Khan were released from a Lahore jail on Thursday. The Punjab government revoked their detention orders, leaders of his Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI) party said. But his elder sister and wife remain behind bars.

Article Title: Pakistan announces schedule for Guru Nanak’s 557th birth anniversary celebrations despite Attari-Wagah closure
Article Text:
Pakistan has maintained that the Kartarpur Corridor remains open from its side (Photo: PTI).

AMRITSAR: Despite the continued closure of the Attari-Wagah international land border following Operation Sindoor, the Pakistan government has announced a programme for the 557th birth anniversary celebrations of Guru Nanak Dev, expecting between 2,300 and 2,700 Sikh pilgrims from India for the November 24 event at Nankana Sahib.Pakistan has also maintained that the Kartarpur Corridor remains open from its side, although pilgrim movement through it continues to be suspended by India.According to Pak media reports, the programme was finalised at a meeting of the Pakistan Sikh Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (PSGPC), chaired by its president and Punjab provincial minister for minority affairs and human rights, Ramesh Singh Arora, to review arrangements for the celebrations.As per the schedule, Indian Sikh pilgrims are expected to arrive in Pakistan through the Attari international border on November 22. The main ceremony will be held on November 24 at Gurdwara Janam Asthan, Nankana Sahib, the birthplace of Guru Nanak Dev. The pilgrims are scheduled to return on December 1.Reacting to Pakistan’s announcement, Sikh scholar Jagdeep Singh said the proposed pilgrimage programme assumes significance amid strained India-Pakistan ties and the continued closure of the Attari-Wagah border after Operation Sindoor.“Keeping the border open would serve the interests of both countries and, above all, make it easier for devotees to visit their historic religious shrines,” said Jagdeep.Interestingly, while Pakistan maintains that the Kartarpur corridor is operational on its side and has expressed readiness to facilitate Sikh devotees, India has suspended pilgrim movement through it since May 2025.In a statement, Arora said Pakistani diplomatic missions had been instructed to facilitate visa issuance for Sikh pilgrims. He also urged India to allow the Sikh sangat to visit its historic shrines.According to reports, the arrangements reviewed at the meeting include air-conditioned buses, accommodation, langar, medical facilities, mineral water and currency exchange services. A Rescue 1122 ambulance will accompany every convoy of 20 buses to meet medical emergencies.
Article Summary: Pakistan has announced a programme for the 557th birth anniversary celebrations of Guru Nanak Dev. It is expecting between 2,300 and 2,700 Sikh pilgrims from India for the November 24 event at Nankana Sahib. Pakistan has also maintained that the Kartarpur Corridor remains open from its side.

Article Title: 'Two eight-year-olds or four four-year-olds': Pakistani cleric's child bride 'joke' sparks outrage
Article Text:
Mufti Tariq Masood (Source: Wikimedia Commons)

Education and women's autonomy

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Pakistani Islamic preacher Mufti Tariq Masood, who commands a large following across social media platforms, has faced criticism over a series of sermons and remarks defending child marriage.In a report published by Daily Mirror Sri Lanka, the influential Deobandi cleric's comments have been reported in detail.One of the remarks highlighted in the report came from a viral video in which Masood joked that if someone could not find a 16-year-old bride, he could provide “two eight-year-olds” or “four four-year-olds”. The comment drew criticism from people who said it trivialised child marriage and normalised the sexualisation of minors.The Daily Mirror said the backlash was dismissed by supporters as a misunderstanding, with the remark defended as a joke taken out of context.The newspaper also pointed to Masood's repeated opposition to statutory minimum marriage-age laws. According to the report, he has argued that Islamic jurisprudence does not prescribe a universal minimum age of 18 and that parents or guardians should retain discretion over when a girl marries.A recurring theme in his sermons, the newspaper said, is the emphasis on physical development and perceived maturity rather than chronological age when determining whether a girl is ready for marriage. The preacher had made remarks discussing the physical suitability of girls aged nine and ten in the context of marital relations. Pakistan as a country has been grappling with child sexual abuse, forced marriages and gender equality and positioning such leaders as popular figures raises extreme concerns.The Daily Mirror also highlighted Masood's remarks on women's education, saying that some of his statements appear to place a husband's authority above a young wife's decision to continue her studies.It further cited comments about women marrying late, including references to them becoming “aunties”, and discussions of the benefits husbands derive from marriage.Masood has also been criticised for presenting early marriage as a way to manage men's sexual desiresMasood's sermons have reportedly become difficult to access after copyright complaints and takedown requests. Critics have alleged that this limits public scrutiny of his statements, while his supporters maintain that some remarks are circulated without their original context.Masood has built a substantial following on YouTube, Facebook and other social media platforms through a preaching style that combines religious instruction with informal language and humour. His reach extends beyond traditional religious institutions, particularly among younger and urban audiences.
Article Summary: Pakistani Islamic preacher Mufti Tariq Masood has faced criticism over a series of sermons and remarks defending child marriage. In a report published by Daily Mirror Sri Lanka, the influential Deobandi cleric's comments have been reported in detail.

Article Title: Pakistan militant attack kills 10 policemen in KPK's Kohat, gunbattle still under way
Article Text:
No militant organisation has claimed responsibility for the attack so far. (FIle photo)

At least 10 police personnel, including two senior officers, were killed in a militant attack in Pakistan's northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province on Wednesday, officials told news agency AP.The attack occurred in Kohat district, where militants targeted vehicles carrying police officers, leading to an exchange of gunfire between the attackers and security forces, local police official Faisal Khan said.Khan confirmed that two senior police officers were among those killed. He added that the gunbattle was still underway, but did not share further details.No militant organisation has claimed responsibility for the attack so far. However, suspicion is likely to centre on the Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), also known as the Pakistani Taliban, which has intensified its attacks on security forces in the region in recent months.Pakistan has witnessed a rise in militant violence over the past few years, with much of it attributed to the TTP. The group is separate from the Afghan Taliban but shares close ties with it. The Afghan Taliban returned to power in Afghanistan in 2021.Islamabad has repeatedly accused Afghanistan's Taliban-led government of providing shelter to TTP fighters operating against Pakistan. Kabul has denied the allegations.
Article Summary: At least 10 police personnel, including two senior officers, were killed in a militant attack in Pakistan's northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. The attack occurred in Kohat district, where militants targeted vehicles carrying police officers, leading to an exchange of gunfire. No militant organisation has claimed responsibility for the attack so far.

Article Title: Pakistan court frames charges against 8, including grandson of deputy PM Ishaq Dar, in gang rape case
Article Text:
Pakistan deput​y PM Ishaq Dar (File photo)​​

A Pakistani court on Wednesday framed charges against eight suspects, including the grandson of deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar, in connection with the gang rape of two foreign women , an official said.All eight accused, including Muhammad Raza Dar, Ishaq Dar's grandson, pleaded not guilty, the official added.“Lahore court judge Rafaqat Ali Gondal framed charges against the suspects, who pleaded not guilty. He directed the prosecution to present its witnesses on December 9 so that the formal trial proceedings could begin,” the official said.Earlier, police in Pakistan's Punjab province had cleared Raza Dar and his four accomplices of charges in the case, instead charging three other employees of Ishaq Dar's grandson of raping the women.The victims were identified as Stephanie Adnana Mau-Arun of the Netherlands and Astrid Robinson Baracho of Venezuela. They were allegedly kidnapped and raped by Raza Dar and his four friends after arriving in Lahore on a business trip in June. Medical examinations confirmed that the women had been raped. They returned to their respective countries after recording their statements.According to the police report, the women met Raza Dar in Singapore in 2025 and invited him to invest in their cryptocurrency business.After receiving returns on his initial investment, he invested more than $500,000. However, the women allegedly failed to provide further returns or repay the amount.In June, Raza Dar invited the women to Pakistan on the pretext of arranging a meeting with another investor. They initially stayed at a hotel in Islamabad and travelled to the hill station of Murree voluntarily.The women were later taken to a house in Lahore's Defence Housing Authority, where they were allegedly held captive and pressured to repay the money. They were forced to transfer $19,500, as per the police report.Armed men guarded the women and threatened them with a knife, a gun and a broken piece of mirror. They also threatened to kill them and sell their body parts if they failed to meet the demands.The women eventually managed to escape after the vehicle in which their alleged captors were taking them to Lahore airport met with an accident.
Article Summary: Pakistani court frames charges against eight suspects in gang rape of two foreign women. All eight accused, including Muhammad Raza Dar, Ishaq Dar's grandson, pleaded not guilty. The victims were identified as Stephanie Adnana Mau-Arun of the Netherlands and Astrid Robinson Baracho of Venezuela.

Article Title: Former Pakistan PM Imran Khan taken to hospital for eye check-up, treatment; shifted back to Adiala Jail
Article Text:
Imran Khan's health sparks concern

Qureshi also hospitalised

Former Pakistan prime minister Imran Khan was taken to hospital for an eye check-up and treatment before being shifted back to prison, news agency Reuters reported on Wednesday, citing officials.Khan, who is lodged in Adiala Jail in Rawalpindi, was taken to the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS), where he also received treatment for blood pressure-related issues, one of the officials said."He had some blood pressure issues ... and was given required treatment last night. He has been shifted back to his prison cell," the person said.The 74-year-old cricketer-turned-politician has been in prison for more than three years after losing power in a no-confidence vote in 2022. He has faced multiple corruption charges, which he denies, alleging that they are politically motivated. The Shehbaz Sharif government has rejected his claims.All but one of Khan's convictions have been suspended or overturned, with appeals pending.His lawyers have repeatedly raised concerns over his health in prison, claiming that his condition has deteriorated and that he has lost significant vision in his right eye.Wednesday's hospital visit is the first known instance of Khan being taken for treatment and subsequently returned to jail since August, when an earlier hospital visit was cut short.Meanwhile, a Pakistani court has directed jail authorities to allow Khan's legal team to meet him and his wife, his party said.Khan's hospital visit comes a day after his close aide and Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) deputy chairman, Shah Mahmood Qureshi, was taken to a hospital in Lahore after collapsing inside his barrack at Kot Lakhpat Jail.According to a prison official, Qureshi suffered a dizzy spell while walking inside his barrack on Monday, injuring his knee and arm in the fall.The 70-year-old former foreign minister was subsequently shifted to the Punjab Institute of Cardiology for treatment and remains hospitalised.Khan, who led Pakistan to its maiden ODI World Cup title in 1992, has been behind bars for more than three years. Concerns over his health and prison conditions have repeatedly been raised by his family, party members and supporters, including former international cricket colleagues.
Article Summary: Imran Khan was taken to hospital for an eye check-up and treatment before being shifted back to prison. The 74-year-old cricketer-turned-politician has been in prison for more than three years. He has faced multiple corruption charges, which he denies, alleging they are politically motivated.

Article Title: Fresh labour unrest hits Bangladesh garment sector
Article Text:

Mujibur's home district gets security boost

Dhaka: Thirteen garment factories shut indefinitely and five others declared one-day holiday as fresh labour unrest hit Bangladesh's key export industry Sunday, a day before the wage board is due to meet to continue consultations on workers' demand for increase in pay.Tear gas and sound grenades were used by police to disperse protesters in Konabari and Mouchak areas in Gazipur - the country's single-largest garment manufacturing hub, around 25 km from Dhaka.Dhaka has sought to describe the unrest, which began in Oct, as an attempt by former PM Sheikh Hasina-led forces to destabilise the country by causing disruptions in a sector that employs more than four million workers and accounts for over 80% export earnings. The charge has been rejected by Awami League.The protests by garment workers - demanding their minimum monthly wage be increased from 12,500 taka (around Rs 9,450) to 30,000 taka (Rs 22,700) - came a day after factory owners warned of indefinite, unpaid closures at factories where workers refused to resume production.Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) said it had deployed 13 platoons of paramilitary personnel to protect factories, alongside police and the elite Special Response Battalion.Six platoons of BGB have been deployed in Gopalganj to maintain law and order and ensure public security. Gopalganj district holds particular political significance as it is the ancestral home of the country's founding leader and Sheikh Hasina father Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman.Meanwhile, Awami League general secretary Obaidul Quader said the party could not be destroyed through a prolonged ban. "Awami League can rise from the ashes as a Phoenix can do," he said in a post on his Facebook account.
Article Summary: Thirteen garment factories shut indefinitely and five others declared one-day holiday. Tear gas and sound grenades were used by police to disperse protesters in Gazipur. Border Guard Bangladesh deployed 13 platoons of paramilitary personnel to protect factories, alongside police and the elite Special Response Battalion.

Article Title: No fresh trial for Hasina in case for which she got death: Prosecutor
Article Text:
Ex-Bangladesh PM Sheikh Hasina

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Dhaka: Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) chief prosecutor Md aminul Islam Sunday rejected suggestions for a fresh trial of former PM Sheikh Hasina in a crimes against humanity case in which she has been sentenced to death.Islam had earlier made it clear that the Hasina has lost her right to appeal and must now face death, as the 30-day window to challenge the ICT verdict has expired.However, his remarks now come in the backdrop of a media report claiming that it had been suggested to Bangladesh that Hasina be given a chance to appeal her case."There is no provision for such a move (fresh trial) under the existing legal framework," Islam told reporters. Without naming any country, he added that "the neighbouring country had been aware of proceedings from the beginning while Hasina was staying there".On if there was a possibility of allowing Hasina to appeal against her conviction, the chief prosecutor said neither govt nor prosecution authority to grant an appeal beyond the provisions permitted by law - International Crimes (Tribunals) Act, 1973, and Rules of Procedure.
Article Summary: Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) chief prosecutor Md aminul Islam Sunday rejected suggestions for a fresh trial of former PM Sheikh Hasina in a crimes against humanity case. Islam had earlier made it clear that the Hasina has lost her right to appeal and must now face death.

Article Title: Factories shut as Bangladesh garment workers intensify protests over minimum wage
Article Text:
Garment workers are demanding a minimum monthly wage of 30,000 taka

What are the workers demanding?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Bangladesh was rocked by fresh labour unrest on Sunday, with 13 garment factories shutting indefinitely and five others declaring a one-day holiday as workers intensified protests demanding a sharp increase in the minimum wage. The disruption came a day before the government-appointed wage board was scheduled to meet to discuss a revised pay structure.Protesting workers gathered in Gazipur's Konabari and Mouchak areas, prompting police to use tear gas and sound grenades to disperse them. Factory owners said around 50 units across the industrial zone were closed, although production continued at most factories.The workers have been protesting for weeks, demanding an increase in their minimum monthly wage from 12,500 taka (around $100) to 30,000 taka (around $240)."Workers made attempts to gather at different locations this morning, but law enforcement personnel prevented them with their prompt actions and remain deployed at every key point in the industrial area," Gazipur Industrial Police Superintendent Amzad Hossain said.Authorities deployed 13 platoons of Border Guard Bangladesh personnel alongside police in riot gear and the elite Special Response Battalion to maintain order and protect factories.Twenty-five executive magistrates were also assigned to oversee security arrangements.Garment workers are demanding a minimum monthly wage of 30,000 taka, arguing that their current earnings are insufficient to meet rising expenses on food, housing, transport and healthcare. Their protests have centred on the demand for a "living wage to survive".The government formed a Minimum Wage Board on November 1 to recommend a revised pay structure. The board aims to finalise its recommendations by the end of November, with the new wages expected to take effect from December 1. Workers are expected to receive their first salaries under the revised structure in January.The Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) said its representatives would attend Monday's meeting to submit their proposal, but warned that its participation in subsequent discussions would depend on the situation.The unrest has raised concerns over export disruptions during the peak production season for spring and summer orders. Factory owners have warned that prolonged shutdowns could delay shipments and lead to cancellations.Bangladesh is the world's second-largest garment exporter after China. The sector employs more than four million workers and accounts for over 80 per cent of the country's export earnings.
Article Summary: Bangladesh rocked by fresh labour unrest on Sunday. 13 garment factories shut indefinitely and five others declared a one-day holiday. The disruption came a day before the government-appointed wage board was scheduled to meet to discuss a revised pay structure. Workers are demanding a minimum monthly wage of 30,000 taka.
